summary: Several mature tools create or consume companion metadata files beside an artifact. They demonstrate concrete mechanisms for portable licensing, media metadata, signatures and provenance, while a general-purpose sidecar convention still needs project-specific schema and drift checks.

items.text: The REUSE tool checks repository licensing metadata and supports the REUSE convention in which an uncommentable file can have an adjacent same-name .license companion. It turns the sidecar into machine-verifiable SPDX evidence rather than an informal note.

darktable writes XMP sidecar files beside input images, storing editing history and metadata while keeping the source image untouched; it can synchronize those companions with its library database. This is a production example of visible, portable sidecars plus a rebuildable index.

Sigstore Cosign signs arbitrary blobs and writes a signature, certificate or verification bundle as separate output that can travel with the artifact. The companion contains cryptographic verification material without modifying the payload.

in-toto-record creates signed .link metadata describing a step's command, materials and products with hashes. Those sidecars make provenance and artifact drift independently verifiable across a supply-chain workflow.
